step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-stage CMOS op-amp with indirect feedback compensation using split PMOS load
step1_figure.description: Two-stage op-amp where the compensation capacitor (Cc = 240 fF) is connected between the output and the low-impedance node between series PMOS transistors M4T and M4B to achieve indirect compensation without extra power dissipation.

open_loop_gain.description: Low-frequency open-loop differential voltage gain (A_OL = gm1 * R1 * gm2 * R2)

equation.explanation: Product of first-stage gain (gm1*R1) and second-stage gain (gm2*R2)
equation.assumptions: Output resistance dominated by channel-length modulation of cascode/split devices

sky130_expected.calculation: With diff pair Id1 = 10 uA, W/L = 50/2 = 25: gm1 = sqrt(2 * 270u * 25 * 10u) ≈ 367 uA/V. Output resistance R1 ≈ ro1 || ro4 ≈ 1 / (2 * lambda * Id) = 1 / (2 * 0.1 * 10u) = 500 kOhm. First-stage gain A1 ≈ 367u * 500k ≈ 183 (45 dB). Second-stage Id2 = 10 uA, gm2 ≈ 150 uA/V, R2 ≈ 500 kOhm -> A2 ≈ 75 (37.5 dB). Total A_OL ≈ 60 dB to 70 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard two-stage CMOS op-amp DC gain in short-channel/130nm CMOS topology.

unity_gain_frequency.description: Frequency where open-loop differential gain equals 0 dB (unity gain)

equation.explanation: Unity-gain frequency set by the input stage transconductance gm1 and indirect compensation capacitor Cc
equation.assumptions: fz and f2 are sufficiently higher than fun

sky130_expected.calculation: fun = 367 uA/V / (2 * pi * 240 fF) ≈ 243 MHz. Using Baker's textbook nominal gm1 = 150 uA/V gives fun = 150 uA/V / (2 * pi * 0.24 pF) ≈ 100 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Cc = 240 fF gives roughly 100 MHz in textbook long-channel model, extending to ~150-240 MHz in SKY130.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin of the open-loop op-amp at unity-gain frequency

equation.explanation: Phase difference from -180 degrees at unity gain frequency
equation.assumptions: Loop is stable with adequate separation between poles and presence of LHP zero

sky130_expected.calculation: With indirect compensation, the zero is in the LHP (Eq. 24.22) which adds positive phase near fun, boosting PM to ~70° - 85°.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Indirect compensation eliminates RHP zero and shifts f2 higher, yielding robust phase margin.

gain_margin.description: Gain margin: negative of open loop gain when phase reaches -180 degrees

equation.explanation: Attenuation below 0 dB at the frequency where phase shift reaches -180 degrees
equation.assumptions: f_180 exists and is beyond fun

sky130_expected.calculation: As stated on page 781, GM is approximately 20 dB to 25 dB for properly compensated op-amps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: High second-pole frequency provides plenty of margin beyond unity gain.

lhp_zero_frequency.description: Frequency of the left-half-plane zero generated by indirect feedback

equation.explanation: Transconductance of the common-gate connection (M4B) divided by 2*pi*Cc

sky130_expected.calculation: For M4B (100/1 PMOS with 10 uA), gm_p ≈ sqrt(2 * 50u * 100 * 10u) ≈ 316 uA/V. fz = 316 uA/V / (2 * pi * 240 fF) ≈ 210 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: LHP zero appears near or slightly above unity-gain frequency fun, providing lead compensation.

second_pole_frequency.description: Second pole frequency in indirect feedback op-amp

equation.formula: f2 ≈ gm2 * Cc / (2 * pi * C1 * (CL + Cc))
equation.explanation: Second pole pushed higher by indirect feedback ratio Cc/(CL + Cc)
equation.assumptions: C1 is input capacitance of stage 2 (~50 fF), CL = 100 fF, Cc = 240 fF

sky130_expected.reasoning: Pushed far higher than conventional Miller compensation.

slew_rate_negative.description: Negative slew rate (high-to-low transition) discharging load and Cc

equation.explanation: Discharge current supplied by sink current source M8 acting on parallel capacitance
equation.assumptions: I_M8 ≈ 10 uA, CL = 1000 fF in Fig 24.24 discussion, or 100 fF for Fig 24.21

sky130_expected.calculation: For Fig 24.24: I_M8 = 10 uA, C_tot = 1.24 pF -> SR- = 10 uA / 1.24 pF ≈ 8 mV/ns = 8 V/us. For CL = 100 fF: SR- = 10 uA / (100 fF + 240 fF) ≈ 29 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Governed by M8 constant current discharging the effective output node capacitance.

equation.explanation: Diff-amp tail current charging compensation capacitor Cc, second stage PMOS pulls up quickly

sky130_expected.reasoning: M7 can source large transient current, limited predominantly by Iss/Cc rate.

settling_time_low_to_high.description: Settling time for low-to-high step input (500 mV to 900 mV)

equation.explanation: Time for output to settle to final voltage during positive step
equation.assumptions: CL = 1 pF as tested in Fig 24.24

sky130_expected.calculation: Fast rise due to small Cc (240 fF) and unconstrained PMOS pull-up M7; textbook reports ~10 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Direct observation from Fig. 24.24 simulation caption.

settling_time_high_to_low.description: Settling time for high-to-low step input (900 mV to 500 mV)

equation.formula: t_settle_hl ≈ delta_V / SR- ≈ 400 mV / 8 mV/ns = 50 ns (simulated ~60 ns)
equation.explanation: High-to-low transition is slew-rate limited by M8 current sink

sky130_expected.calculation: delta_V / SR = 400 mV / (8 V/us) ≈ 50 ns, plus settling time gives ~60 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Direct observation from Fig. 24.24 simulation caption.

cmrr.description: Common-Mode Rejection Ratio of the op-amp

equation.explanation: Ratio of differential gain to common-mode gain determined by the input differential pair

sky130_expected.calculation: CMRR = 20 * log10(gm1 * 2 * ro_tail) ≈ 50 dB as noted on page 789.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Differential pair with cascode NMOS tail current source M6T/M6B achieves > 50 dB CMRR.

power_dissipation.description: Total quiescent power consumption of the op-amp core and bias generator

equation.explanation: Static power consumption from VDD = 1.8V supply
equation.assumptions: Diff pair = 20 uA, second stage = 10 uA, bias branches ≈ 40-50 uA

sky130_expected.calculation: Total current ≈ 70 uA to 90 uA at 1.8 V -> P ≈ 126 uW to 162 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Supply voltage 1.8V with microamp-level branch currents.

step3_testbench.description: Ngspice testbench verifying AC parameters (gain, unity-gain frequency, phase margin, CMRR), transient slew rate / settling response, and DC power dissipation for the Fig. 24.21 op-amp.
